steps.text: Place chicken breasts into a plastic zipper bag with soy sauce, seal the bag, and marinate in refrigerator for 30 minutes. While chicken is marinating, place bacon in a large, deep skillet, and cook over medium-high heat, occasionally turning until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on a paper towel-lined plate, and set aside. Spread cut sides of hamburger buns with butter.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.

Remove chicken from soy sauce, and discard excess soy sauce. Place chicken breasts onto the preheated grill, and grill until chicken shows good grill marks, is no longer pink inside, and juices run clear, 4 to 5 minutes per side. When chicken is almost done, brush each piece generously on both sides with teriyaki sauce to finish grilling. Place a slice of Swiss cheese on each chicken breast, and cover with a lid to help cheese melt onto chicken.
While chicken is grilling, spread buns open on the grill and cook until toasted and showing grill lines, about 2 minutes. Set buns aside.

To assemble, spread grilled sides of each bun with mayonnaise, and top each bottom bun with a cooked chicken breast, 1 1/2 slices of bacon, a slice of pineapple, a slice from a head of lettuce, a slice of tomato, and top bun.

raw_recipe.headline: Aloha Chicken Burgers
raw_recipe.description: For these Hawaiian chicken burgers, grilled teriyaki chicken breasts are topped with pineapple slices, bacon, Swiss cheese, and sandwich fixings.

video.description: Enjoy your favorite tropical flavors on a juicy chicken burger and experience an island getaway in every bite! First marinate chicken breast in a simple marinade of soy sauce, then cook bacon and butter hamburger buns. Grill chicken breasts, taking care to slather them with a good helping of teriyaki sauce before they’re done. Then melt Swiss cheese over each and grill your hamburger buns. Assemble your sandwiches and top with mayonnaise, pineapple rings, iceberg lettuce and tomato. Serve hot with onion rings or fries and have a tasty meal!

review.reviewBody: I used ground turkey patties because my family doesn't like to eat chicken breasts in a sandwich. Very tasty and everyone agreed they would eat them again. Grill the pineapple too and if you want an extra treat put the pineapple in a bowl with its juice and brown sugar before placing it on the grill, then put it on the sandwich.

Quick, and great! Made a double recipe, the family loved it! Soy sauce alone for a marinade would have been too salty, so I cut it with 1 Tbs brown sugar and a 1/3 cup of pineapple juice. I halved and tenderized my chicken breasts with a meat tenderizer as well. That helped result in a very tender chicken fillet. Will make again!

Cooked the chicken in the crockpot with low sodium soy sauce and brown sugar, chicken fell apart somewhat so I brushed them with teriyaki sauce and cheese, place on foil and melted cheese in the oven. Sprinkled pineapple rings with brown sugar and grilled them. Followed all other steps exactly. My family loved it and will make these again.

Cooked the chicken in the crockpot with low sodium soy sauce and brown sugar, chicken fell apart somewhat so I brushed them with teriyaki sauce and cheese, place on foil and melted cheese in the oven. Sprinkled pineapple rings with brown sugar and grilled them. Followed all other steps exactly. My family loved it and will make these again.

WOW! That is what my husband and I both said, which is A LOT coming from my husbands mouth! lol The flavor combo in these are so delicious! Instead of marinating the chicken in soy sauce, I used more teriyaki to marinate them in and had extra to baste after grilling. I also grilled the pineapple and basted them with the teriyaki sauce. I did mix part of the juice from the pineapple, in with the teriyaki sauce, to meld the flavors more together. Also I do suggest if your chicken breasts are extra thick like mine were, to pound and flatten them out to a medium thickness, to be more uniform in shape. That way when you put them on your burger, they will sit better on the sandwich. Delicious Delicious! Thank you for the recipe! This will be a staple in our house!

Pretty good! Made it on the stove. I sliced the chicken into strips to cook faster. Put olive oil and a little soy sauce in the bottom of the pan and cooked the chicken on med hi heat, last 10 mins put some teriyaki sause on them. Turned out great!

I grilled the pineapple slices which added to the open-face presentation. Not being a big fan of bacon (or Spam), I omitted it. I found that a single slice of Swiss cheese wasn't sufficient to influence the taste of sandwich and recommend two slices of Swiss or trying a less mild cheese for anyone trying this burger. Overall, I found this to be a pretty bland sandwich.

Easy to make and very tasty! Followed the recipe, added brown sugar to the soy sauce, as others had suggested and to the pineapple as it grilled. YUM! Only other change I made was to cook the bacon in the oven, as I was making double of the recipe. Everyone in the family loved it!
These were mmm good. My husband actually used the word "Amazing." I used canned pineapple and poured some of the juice into the marinade. I also cooked it all on my stove in a cast iron skillet.

I marinated the chicken in a bottled BBQ marinade (Mama Sita's, Philippino-style) instead of soy as I was low. Let it marinade for about an hour. Didn't butter or grill the bread- I used these new bun 'thins' that are available instead of the traditional ones. I made my own teriyaki-style sauce using 'Baked Teriyaki Chicken' from AR. I used grill pan on the stove-top, then finished them off in the oven at 400F for 20 minutes. I used much more teriyaki sauce than called for for basting. We thought the pineapple was a bit much and would skip it next time, though I went the extra mile and caramelized the rings. I think the mayo can become optional if you use more teriyaki than called for for the chicken- Some guests used mayo, other didn't at all. It was well-liked. Served it with 'Hawaiian Coleslaw' from AR.

This recipe looked so good I could hardly wait to make it. I sliced the chicken breasts in half lengthwise to make them thinner, and instead of using bacon I topped each one with a slice of ham, then pineapple and cheese. I served them without a bun, with rice as a side. I made these for company and they were a hit! I'll definitely make them again! So easy and so delicious!
So delicious! I had to use sugar free teriyaki and canned pineapple sugar free. It’s yummy and I bet if you had sugar it would be even better!
A little salty

Hubby gave it a 4 & I think it is a 5 star. Will make again but with these changes. We'll probably use can slice pineapple or if a fresh one slice a lot thinner. We'll also cu breast in half for thinner pieces & share a chicken breast. With a full breast, even sliced for easier grilling it was to much. The fresh sliced pineapple was also to think so everything slid around & was way to messy. We took others suggestion & used 1/8c soy sauce & 1/8c plus of pineapple juice. Initially I thought the marinade was to overpowering with soy sauce. We'll have to cut the marinade to compensate for using the 1 chicken breast. Like others you may want to add a tish of brown sugar.
Tasted okay. A little salty.
My family loved this burger so much
So delicious! The whole family gave it a thumbs up.
This was delicious!!!!!
Awesome. I did add a little bit of brown sugar to the soy sauce as most reviewers also had. Thanks for sharing
I made these at a family cookout and got rave reviews. It makes a huge sandwich. I served it with a Hawaiian Mac salad I found on the internet.
